mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.00% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.00% in a month
regime_hint: Rising inflationary bias in the Fed’s policy framework
failure_condition: Over a 6-month window, 20-day forward returns after such rate spikes are not statistically different from pre-rate hike periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2.0% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that prompt the market to discount future equities more aggressively, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: Mid-cycle inflation acceleration detected by core CPI
failure_condition: In 20 such inflation spikes, the 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative (average p-value > 0.25 across windows).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PAYEMS and a decline in UNRATE over the same month indicates strengthening labor market conditions without wage moderation, which elevates equity risk premia and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market tightening without wage inflation
failure_condition: During 10 such labor cycle shifts, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (bootstrap p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in GDPC1 (real private consumption) above the prior quarter’s average, coupled with a positive HOUST reading, predicts a temporary boost in investor optimism that lifts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > QoQ average and HOUST > prior month in the same month
failure_condition: Across 8 such events, the 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the mean of neutral months (p > 0.15 in a two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO below the prior 6-month average, in conjunction with elevated RSAFS, signals weakening manufacturing capacity and rising supply-side risks, which tends to depress S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 6-month rolling avg and RSAFS increases in the same month
failure_condition: In 5 such supply shocks, the 60-day forward returns are not meaningfully lower than during neutral supply cycles (median p-value > 0.30).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in PAYEMS for three consecutive months suggests weakening labor demand, which raises uncertainty and elevates equity risk aversion, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: During 4 such labor weakness episodes, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month’s average (p > 0.20).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1.00% for two consecutive months during a period of rising UNRATE, the low-rate environment persists and supports equity valuation expansion, predicting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.00% for 2 consecutive months and UNRATE rising
regime_hint: Low-rate hold in rising inflation context
failure_condition: In 7 such low-rate regimes, the 60-day forward returns are not consistently higher than the mean of high-rate regimes (median p-value > 0.35).

mechanism_narrative: A long-term upward trend in CPIAUCSL (5-year moving average) is associated with higher inflation expectations and tighter credit conditions, which tend to compress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: Persistent inflation trend over multi-year horizon
failure_condition: Across 12 such inflation-trend episodes, the 20-day forward returns are not systematically negative (average p-value > 0.40).
